problems.title: Graph scalability: chains, grids and random networks
problems.summary: Generated thermal graphs from 100 nodes up (to 100,000 under --full), on the serial, thread-pool and partitioned backends, under Euler node by node and Runge–Kutta 4: the same numbers bit for bit on every backend, the engine's work as counted, the method's exact steps to rounding, and the exact solution's error; under --full, wall time, throughput, peak memory, parallel speed-up and the time to load, compile and solve.

checks.name: backendBitDifferences
checks.description: Sampled values that differ, bit for bit, between the serial backend and the thread-pool or partitioned backend, over every graph, size and method

checks.name: backendWorkDifferences
checks.description: Runs whose reported work (global steps, node substeps, contributions evaluated) differs from the serial run of the same graph and method

checks.name: workCountDifferences
checks.description: Work counts that differ from what the model implies: N substeps a global step; each contribution once a substep under Euler, once a stage under Runge–Kutta 4

checks.name: backendNotAsRequested
checks.description: Runs whose effective backend or worker count is not the one requested (so a parallel backend really ran in parallel)

checks.name: eulerExactStepsDifference
checks.description: explicit Euler: largest difference from the method's exact steps (closed form for the chain and grid, stepped independently for the random network), relative to the largest starting temperature

checks.name: eulerExactSolutionError
checks.description: explicit Euler: largest error against the exact solution, K (chain and grid at every size, the random network by the matrix exponential at 100 nodes), h = 0.02 s to t = 1 s

checks.name: rungeKutta4ExactStepsDifference
checks.description: Runge–Kutta 4: largest difference from the method's exact steps (closed form for the chain and grid, stepped independently for the random network), relative to the largest starting temperature

checks.name: rungeKutta4ExactSolutionError
checks.description: Runge–Kutta 4: largest error against the exact solution, K (chain and grid at every size, the random network by the matrix exponential at 100 nodes), h = 0.02 s to t = 1 s

checks.name: randomHeatConservation
checks.description: Random network: largest drift of the total heat Σ C_i T_i from Konjugate's own states, relative to Σ C_i |T_i(0)|, over every size and method

notes: Every backend gives the same bits because every backend reads the same snapshot (Euler) or the same immutable stage vector (Runge–Kutta 4) and commits its results in a fixed order (docs/parallelExecution.md). The accuracy run uses small graphs; --full measures the same families up to 100,000 nodes, with the time it takes.

Not measured at 1,000,000 nodes: A project of a million nodes is about 1.45 GB of JSON (about 1,450 bytes a node with its two relationships), more than one JavaScript string can hold, so the project encoder cannot write it; the engine's validation alone would take about six minutes (about 0.33 ms a node, measured at 10,000 and 100,000 nodes), and the 8 GB machine these benchmarks were written on could not hold the document while the engine parses it.
